missionPremise: The PDF masthead logo is a hand redrawing of the brand asset rather than the asset itself, because hauska-engine contains no brand asset for the report chrome to reference.
completionPredicate: The masthead and running-header marks are DERIVED from the canonical hauska-map asset with a recorded source path and version, so the two cannot silently drift; proportions match canon exactly; any paper-only colour substitution is explicit, minimal and justified against a stated contrast ratio on --ss-paper.
scopeBasis: Report chrome only. No sheet body content is touched, verified by git diff --name-only.
falsifier: PRE-REGISTERED FOUR, SCORED HONESTLY. (1) Numeric geometry diff against the canonical SVG - predicted exact match on stroke-width, dot radius, tick length and viewBox after the change, with only a colour substitution remaining. CORRECT: measured from the generated PDF, four ticks at 7.1053pt each = 18*(30/76) and stroke 1.5789pt = 4*(30/76), all four straddling the ring. (2) Brand version - predicted v2 does NOT redefine the mark, so the v1 logo files are current canon. CORRECT, and verified two independent ways rather than by reading the docs alone. (3) PDF decode - predicted the wordmark would NOT decode, on the pdf-lib StandardFonts ToUnicode hazard the dispatch named. WRONG. The chrome deliberately uses fontkit-embedded Barlow for exactly that reason, documented in report-chrome.ts's own ChromeFonts note, and 'SMART SITE' decodes cleanly out of a generated PDF. I predicted the hazard without checking whether the code had already been fixed for it. (4) Body content - predicted zero change. CORRECT.
contradicted: FIVE things I expected or was told, that the evidence overturned. (a) The dispatch's delta table understates the defect: it reads as a weight-and-size difference, but the mark is ASYMMETRIC - N/S/W ticks are 14 units and float DETACHED 4 units clear of the ring while E is 34 and crosses it. `outer = 76 - inner` mixes a 76-unit space into a 96-unit one and the source SVG's translate(10,10) was dropped. Found by reading the write path, not by measuring output. (b) The dispatch lists one stroke-width delta (4 vs 3); there are TWO rings with TWO different wrong weights - MARK_RING 3 and WORDMARK_RING 2, the latter 60.4% thin. (c) report-chrome-tokens.ts records --ss-print-gold #B87116 as 4.6:1 on paper. It is 3.752:1. It fails the 4.5:1 normal-text floor it claimed and passes only the 3:1 large-text floor. My own instrument's self-test failed on this before I trusted the number, which is how it surfaced. (d) `assets/logo.svg`, cited in the design brief as 'the untouched original', DOES NOT EXIST anywhere - checked doc_repo by find, hauska-map origin/main by git ls-tree, and hauska-map's full history by git log --all --diff-filter=A. (e) My own first instrument was wrong: a bash heredoc silently collapsed [\\d] to [d], producing a parser that matched no digits and would have reported a clean parse. It was caught only because the instrument self-tests in both directions and failed its POSITIVE case.

Whether hauska-map intends these two SVGs to remain the mark. The lock pins the asset as of b360138 and detects local tampering; it CANNOT detect the owning repo moving on. Nothing notifies this repo of an upstream logo change.

The 17.9pt figure used to justify #B87116 under the large-text floor is the wordmark's computed size (34 * 30/76 = 13.42pt at the PDF's own scale, ~17.9px at 96dpi). It is comfortably above the 14pt-bold threshold either way, but the threshold comparison was not independently re-derived against a typographic authority.

Two pre-existing tests are flaky under full-suite parallel load and pass in isolation: feasibility-narrative-wiring (30s timeout) and manifest-is-load-bearing (two renders of the same manifest differed, 591901 vs 591882 bytes). The second is a REAL nondeterminism in the PDF writer that its own test is designed to catch, and it is worth a row. A deterministic diff cannot cause run-to-run variance, and the full suite passed 490/490 with these changes in place on another run, so I do not attribute either to this change - but I did not bisect against the base commit to prove it.

LESSON: A bash heredoc with <<'EOF' still collapsed [\\d] to [\d] in this environment, yielding a JS regex of [d] that matches no digits. Write instruments with the Write tool, never a heredoc, and self-test them in BOTH directions. This is the ENFORCEMENT 'lost its backslashes' instance recurring verbatim.

packages/engine-core's own `tsc --noEmit` is NOT the repo's typecheck. packages/retrieval compiles engine-core's sources under noUncheckedIndexedAccess and is stricter. Run repo-wide `pnpm typecheck` before pushing or CI finds it for you.

An OPTIONAL interface field means the compiler cannot catch its omission from a return object. I built the whole wordmark and forgot to return it; tsc was silent and only a test caught it. Where a field is always present for a given input shape, prefer a split type over an optional.
drawTrackedText in render.ts returns the ABSOLUTE RIGHT EDGE, not a width. Reading the signature took ten seconds; assuming it would have shipped a displaced wordmark.

The report chrome's fonts are fontkit-embedded Barlow, NOT pdf-lib StandardFonts, specifically so drawn text carries a ToUnicode CMap and decodes. The StandardFonts hazard is real but was already fixed here - check whether a documented hazard still applies before predicting it will bite.
DEAD-END: npx tsx -e for a quick module probe hung past 180s twice in this worktree. vitest with a throwaway test file is the fast path for exercising a TS module here.

Patching a file by literal multi-line string match fails in this repo: core.autocrlf=true means the working tree is CRLF. Use a line-ending-agnostic regex, and always guard a patch with an explicit no-op check so a vacuous violation cannot be mistaken for a passing control.
